title: Upcountry water shortage conservation plan
summary: Upcountry residents weighed in on January 24, 2024, on a draft water conservation plan, using stickers to mark priorities and comment cards or email for more ideas. At the time, the department hoped to finish the plan by the end of March, after feedback from its advisory board and the state Water Commission. The plan aims to cut water use 20% by 2040, and staff said a watering-schedule ordinance could reach the council in March at the earliest.

timeline.text: Staff said the earliest a new ordinance bill could go to the council is March.
The plan goes to the department's advisory board and the state Water Commission for feedback.
Residents can still send ideas on comment cards or by email after the meeting.
Attendees got four stickers each to mark which measures the department should prioritize.
One proposed ordinance (a county law) could set watering schedules by time of day or day of the week.
The consultant said smart meters could save between 8 and 15% of water demand.
An engineering consultant described 19 possible conservation measures in nine categories.
The department is aiming for a 20% water conservation goal by 2040.
Staff said low-flow fixture programs have saved about 300,000 gallons of water per day so far.
The department hopes to finish the plan by the end of March.
Staff said new water supply has become more and more expensive, so using existing water more efficiently helps avoid or delay new sources.

fromCommunityMeetings.quote: And this plan is, we intend to have it completed by the end of March.
fromCommunityMeetings.about: Gives the department's target for finishing the countywide water shortage and conservation plan that Upcountry residents also commented on.

fromCommunityMeetings.quote: So if we set a pretty aggressive goal of 20% for the systems that have the larger demand and see most the growth, which would be the central upcountry in Lahaina, and for the smaller rural system, a 10% goal, these are really efficient what is already, we could bring that gallons per day per capita down from 249 to 200 gallons per capita per day. And we think it's possible with the right portfolio of conservation measures.
fromCommunityMeetings.about: Explains the proposed conservation targets in the plan, including a 20% goal for the Upcountry system.

fromCommunityMeetings.quote: Back to the way Haiku North Shore is grouped with upcountry. Like with this recent drought restrictions, my personal situation is my driveway desperately needs to be power washed.
fromCommunityMeetings.about: A Haʻikū resident describes how being grouped with the Upcountry system under drought restrictions affects them despite heavy local rain.

fromCommunityMeetings.quote: So, even in operational issues, we end up having a true shortage in Haiku, even during rain, because the well is down for various reasons for an extended time.

fromCommunityMeetings.quote: Okay, so we're trying to clear some of our wells at Hamakua Popo to use that if we need to.

fromCommunityMeetings.quote: You kind of already answered it, but the request I know has been received for people that are still dealing with burn-affected properties and if they can be exempted from the water situations right now, like when Army Corps goes through and hydro-seeds properties at the end, our understanding is that's the responsibility of the property owner to keep that irrigated.
